subject: Recap: Redwood dedicated capacity discussion — Finlytics needs & next steps
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@finlytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>

Subject: Recap: Redwood dedicated capacity discussion — Finlytics needs & next steps

Hi Alex — thanks again for taking the time today. Short recap of what we discussed and the items we agreed to follow up on. Please confirm or correct any numbers below so we can lock in a proposed config and SOW.

Summary of Finlytics needs (as discussed)
- Workload: document parsing + extractive Q&A + analytics pipelines (mix of short and medium prompts).
- Estimated steady-state tokens / month: ~200M–300M (per your estimate).
- Peak day tokens: ~20M (spiky events tied to batch reports).
- Target unit economics: aiming for ~$600–$800 per 1M tokens (goal to land under $700 if possible).
- Interest: Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU pool) for predictable latency and data isolation.
- Desired GPU(s): preference for H100s due to latency/throughput on long-context models — mentioned potentially starting with 4x H100.
- Throughput targets: support ~100–150k tokens/sec aggregate to meet peak concurrency (back-of-envelope).

Next steps we agreed:
1) We (Redwood) to send a pricing options PDF that maps reserved pool sizes (2x / 4x / 8x H100 and A100 variants) to monthly costs and effective $/1M token under multiple utilization scenarios. (Attached: Redwood-Dedicated-Pricing-Options-Q1-2027.pdf)
2) Marcus will provide estimated throughput numbers and sizing guidance for H100 vs A100 for your expected mix.
3) Finlytics to confirm which steady-state token number (pick a conservative target) and any firm budget constraints so we can build the SOW.
4) If all good, plan a 4–6 week pilot (performance + integration) and then convert to reserved capacity.

Questions for you (please reply inline):
- Confirm steady-state monthly tokens to use for pricing (200M, 250M, 300M?).
- Is $600–$800/1M an absolute upper bound or a target range?
- Any compliance/legal requirements we should flag for Private deployment (if this matters for the SOW)?

Attachments: Redwood-Dedicated-Pricing-Options-Q1-2027.pdf (pricing scenarios)

Thanks — I’ll follow up with Marissa and Marcus’ notes and a proposed cadence for the SOW draft.

Best,
Dylan Brooks

Thanks, Dylan — that matches our notes. A few clarifications from my side: 

- Steady-state: let's price against 250M tokens/month as the baseline (we suspect steady-state will be ~250M; spikes up to ~20M/day).
- Budget range: $600–$800/1M is the negotiation range but our procurement target is closer to $650/1M if we can get firm SLAs for latency. So treat $650 as the target for modeling.
- GPUs: we did ask the infra team; they prefer H100 for lower latency on our long-context models. Starting with 4x H100 feels right as an initial reserved pool subject to throughput confirmation.
- Compliance: Finlytics will require SOC 2 evidence and network isolation for production-ingest (we will share the vendor questionnaire separately).

Happy to have you send the pricing scenarios and the SOW draft. Timeline: Procurement approval by 4/15 would be ideal.

Alex — looping in formal pricing options. Per Dylan's note and your confirmation on 250M baseline and target $650/1M, here are two quick commercial options (high level):

Option A (Conservative) — 4x H100 reserved pool
- Monthly commitment: $48,000/month (reserved capacity, H100 family)
- Assumed utilization for unit price calc: 70% effective (accounting for batch windows, downtime, dev usage)
- Effective unit price (250M tokens/month): ~$685 / 1M tokens
- SLA: 99.9% availability, 95th pctl tail-latency target included in SOW
- Included: standard observability, logging, SOC2 evidence package (redacted), monthly business review

Option B (Aggressive / higher utilization) — 4x H100 + committed burst credits
- Monthly commitment: $56,000/month (higher committed throughput + burst buffers)
- Assumed utilization: 85% effective
- Effective unit price (250M tokens/month): ~$560 / 1M tokens
- Includes negotiated burst allowance for peak days and priority routing

Notes/assumptions:
- The effective $/1M above assumes Redwood's prefix/KV caching and batching typical for your workload; if your workload has very low cache hit rate we will revisit.
- We can provide A100 alternatives (lower sticker, lower latency) if budget dictates — Marcus will include throughput delta.

Next steps:
- Marcus: can you confirm throughput numbers per GPU for our target model family and recommended concurrency?
- Alex: confirm if Option A or B looks closer to the budget target; if neither, give a target monthly commitment and I’ll iterate.
- Dylan: I’ll draft the SOW & timeline (4–6 week pilot) and share a preview by EOD tomorrow.

Attachments: Redwood-Dedicated-Pricing-Options-Q1-2027.pdf (pricing scenarios), SOW-draft-Redwood-Finlytics.docx (placeholder)

Thanks — Marissa

Subject: Re: Recap: Redwood dedicated capacity discussion — throughput & GPU guidance

Alex / team — some quick sizing guidance based on the model family you described (mix of short prompts and medium-context extraction). High-level numbers (approximate, will validate in pilot):

H100 (fp16 / sparsity-optimized path) 
- Single H100 (per our internal benchmarks on similar LLMs): sustained generation throughput ~25k–40k tokens/sec depending on sequence length and batch sizes. For mixed workload assume ~30k tokens/sec per GPU.
- 4x H100 aggregate throughput: ~120k tokens/sec (conservative). That maps to ~7.2M tokens/minute, ~432M tokens/hour at continuous run (but real workloads are bursty).

A100 comparison:
- Single A100: ~18k–28k tokens/sec (rough average 22k tokens/sec). 4x A100 aggregate ~88k tokens/sec.

Operational sizing notes:
- If average request size is ~500 tokens and target concurrency is 40 qps, that implies ~20k tokens/sec sustained — 4x H100 covers that with headroom for spikes.
- Caching: enabling prefix/KV caching for repeat queries can reduce token generation by ~15–30% which improves effective $/1M.
- Pilot: recommend a 1-week perf run with a mirrored workload on 2x and 4x H100 to validate latency and cost assumptions. We'll provide a perf report with p99 latency and token/sec curves.

Action items from engineering:
- I'll schedule the perf test once Finlytics confirms which pool size to mirror (2x vs 4x).
- Provide a short runbook for model pinning/rollbacks during the pilot.

— Marcus
